name: Hard Bargain
note: R8.13, Advanced Missions SSD p.144. The Orion war cruiser, and the only Orion in the book whose point value prints as a SINGLE number (115) rather than EPV/BPV - it is a warship, not a converted trader. Cloak cost prints 15/4; the 4 applies only to a ship with no warp engines, so cloakCost is 15. The sheet states its HET standing outright - 'THIS SHIP HAS TWO HET BONUSES UNDER (C6.521). IT IS NOT NIMBLE.' - hence bonusHets 2 with nimble false, two separate facts on one hull. THREE ADJACENT CENTERLINE MOUNTS (A, B, C) plus one on each wing (D on the LS, E on the RS): the first three-mount run in the data, and the first real exercise of the run semantics, since A-B and B-C are adjacent while A-C is not. NO PLUS REFIT: the CA's sheet carries a stippled swatch legended 'SHADED BOXES ARE ADDED BY THE PLUS REFIT' and this one carries neither legend nor stipple, so every box printed counts. Its 30/30/24/24/24/30 is exactly the CA's POST-plus shielding, which fits a Y168 hull built to the later standard. Phaser arcs combine the box label with the letter printed beside it: 'PH-1-FA' plus 'L' is FA+L, 'PH-3-RA' plus 'R' is RA+R (owner, 2026-10-20). So the port pairs reach one hexside further to port and the starboard pairs to starboard, and orion/ca.json's forward Ph-1 read the same way. The one hull still to recheck under this reading is orion/cr.json, whose rear Ph-3 carry a bare RA. NOT MODELLED, all for the same reason - they depend on what goes into the option mounts, so no static field can hold them: DERFACS free in Y168 if a disruptor of range 30+ is fitted; one extra reload in Y175 for drone or plasma racks fitted to the mounts; the Y170 plasma carronade and the sabot refit, both Module R10. The MINELAYER REFIT (R8.R1) is also unentered - its text is in neither the Master Rulebook nor this book's text layer - but M9.21 says its racks go in the SHUTTLE BAYS and are limited to one mine per turn per BAY (not per box), and M9.16 says a ship given mine racks this way is NOT thereby a minesweeper. Each cargo box holds 25 points of cargo (G25.12).
